findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix AC #1's verification command to a surface that actually reports direct-child status — e.g. `rebar list --parent=facb-44c3-2ada-41ee --status=open,in_progress --output json` returns an empty array — instead of `rebar list-descendants … --output json`, which accepts no --output flag and emits type-bucketed ids with no status.
evidence: docs/cli-reference.md:306 — 'Usage: rebar list-descendants <root_ticket_id>   (BFS walk bucketed by type, JSON)'; no --output flag documented
src/rebar/_engine_support/descendants.py:77-85 — list_descendants_cli parses only argv[0]; a trailing '--output json' is dropped; output is unconditionally json.dumps(...)

src/rebar/_engine_support/descendants.py:38-74 + src/rebar/schemas/list_descendants.schema.json:8-14 — buckets {epics,stories,tasks,bugs,parents_with_children} contain only ticket-ID strings; no per-child status and no direct-vs-descendant distinction
MATCH/MISMATCH classification: MISMATCH (Verified against --help/docs and source)
Achievable alternative exists: docs/cli-reference.md:288-294 — `rebar list --parent=<id> --status=open,in_progress` where --parent filters to DIRECT children and --status filters lifecycle state
findings.finding: AC #1's verification command `rebar list-descendants facb-44c3-2ada-41ee --output json reports no open or in_progress direct child` names a CLI capability the command does not have: `list-descendants` takes only `<root_ticket_id>` (no `--output json` flag — it is silently ignored), emits a BFS of ALL descendants bucketed by TYPE as ticket-ID strings with NO status field, and does not distinguish DIRECT children — so it cannot report 'no open or in_progress direct child.'
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC #1 ('Every direct child is closed; rebar list-descendants … --output json reports no open or in_progress direct child.')
scenarios: Integration worktree runs AC #1 verbatim at land time; the command ignores --output json and returns type-bucketed id lists with no status, so the operator cannot mechanically confirm 'no open or in_progress direct child'
An open direct child is silently not flagged because the command surfaces no status, letting the epic close with an unfinished child
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC #1 recipe with: 'Every direct child is closed; `rebar list --parent=facb-44c3-2ada-41ee --status=open,in_progress --output json` returns an empty array.' (`--parent` = direct children; `--status` filters lifecycle state.)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Close the drift window between the green-on-origin-main measurement and the atomic merge-back: specify a re-fetch/rebase-and-remeasure loop immediately before submit (or a submit-time CI gate that re-runs the newly-enforced gates against the post-merge tip), so no gate can land red on the origin/main it actually merges into.
evidence: AC: 'Before the final merge-back lands, `git fetch origin` is run and every gate ... exits 0 against the **current** `origin/main` tip'
AC: 'including any introduced by `origin/main` drift after each story's measured baseline commit ... is resolved ... before the corresponding gate is landed'
Approach: 'merge the completed branch atomically to main' — atomicity is claimed for the merge, not for the (measure-then-submit) sequence
Comment on epic notes real drift already occurred: 'baseline 0f5dbc88b has drifted to 34998a2ca8' — confirming main advances during this epic's lifetime
findings.finding: The green-on-origin-main enforcement is specified as a pre-land check ('git fetch origin' then each gate exits 0 against the current origin/main tip 'before the corresponding gate is landed'), but the delivery mechanism merges the feature branch to main as a separate atomic no-ff submit. Nothing in the plan closes the window between measuring 'green on current origin/main' and executing the submit: origin/main can advance again in that interval, introducing new ratchet-family diagnostics (or C901 drift) that the just-verified gates never saw, so a gate can land red on the origin/main it actually merges into. This is a check-then-act race between the drift-reconciliation check and the atomic merge-back.
findings.location: Approach section + the two 'green-on-origin-main' ACs (the <!-- green-on-origin-main AC --> block)
scenarios: Reviewer verifies `make lint`/`make typecheck`/`config-check`/C901 wrapper all exit 0 against origin/main tip T1; an unrelated change lands on origin/main (tip T2) adding a new DTZ or C901-over-baseline diagnostic; the no-ff merge-back is then submitted and main is now red on a gate this epic just enforced.
A concurrent RUF-introducing change merges to main between fetch and submit, so RUF100/RUF gate is green at check time but red post-merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach: the merge-back is gated by a submit-time re-check — immediately before submit, re-run `git fetch origin`, rebase the merge-back onto the current origin/main tip, and re-run the four newly-enforced gates (C901 wrapper, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `config-check`) on that rebased tip; if any gate reports new/increased drift, resolve it (or capture it in the C901 baseline) and repeat until the submit races no further advance. Rely on Gerrit submit-time CI re-verification as the backstop.
